prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” HVAC company for every Atlanta homeowner — the best choice depends on your exact location, budget, the size/type of system you need, brand preferences, and whether you want long warranties or fast availability. I can help you find the best fit. First, here are practical steps and what to look for so you can pick a reliable contractor:

What to require from any installer
- Valid license, insurance, and permits. Verify they carry liability and workers’ comp and will pull required local permits.
- NATE- or manufacturer-certified technicians.
- A Manual J load calculation (not just “match the old tonnage”).
- Written, itemized quote showing equipment make/model, SEER rating, refrigerant type, labor warranty, and any manufacturer warranty.
- Clear start/completion dates and payment schedule.
- Post-install paperwork (permit sign-off, system paperwork, manuals, start-up records).
- Energy-efficiency advice (SEER ratings, heat pump vs. central AC) and rebate info.

How to choose
- Get at least 3 written quotes for the same scope of work (same capacity, SEER, etc.).
- Compare installed price, warranties (parts and labor), and included services (e.g., thermostat, ductwork repairs).
- Prefer companies with local references and a track record in Atlanta (years in business, positive Google/Yelp/BBB reviews).
- Ask about seasonal promotions, financing, and whether they handle permits/inspection.

Questions to ask contractors
1. Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide license number and proof?
2. Will you perform a Manual J load calculation?
3. What brand/models do you recommend and why?
4. What is included in your labor warranty and for how long?
5. Who will perform the work — your employees or subcontractors?
6. Will you pull all required permits and handle inspections?
7. What refrigerant will the unit use? (R-410A vs newer blends)
8. Can you provide references from recent installs in my neighborhood?
9. What is the expected timeline from start to finish?
10. Do you offer maintenance plans and/or customer follow-up?

Red flags
- Very low ball quotes without an on-site assessment.
- Pressure to sign immediately or insistence on large up-front cash payments.
- Refusal to provide license, insurance, or written contract.
- No clear warranty or skipped permitting.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC contractors near your Atlanta ZIP code and give a short, current list (with pros/cons and review summaries).
- Or help you compare 3 quotes you receive.

Which would you prefer? If you want me to look up companies, tell me your ZIP code and whether you prefer certain brands, budget range, or urgency.
